argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0209d: meeting "d" (detailed design) of series SY0209.

PROJECT
The team is designing a children's educational tablet case.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Project Manager (PM)  Laura  present
B  Marketing Expert (ME)  Tomasz  present
C  User Interface designer (UI)  Priya  present
D  Industrial Designer (ID)  Ben  ABSENT, never speaks

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0209a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, the team introduced themselves, and she presented the project: a case for the company's existing Learnly seven-inch children's educational tablet. She gave the financial targets of a selling price of 25 Euros and a maximum production cost of 12.50 Euros per case, excluding packaging. The team agreed to keep the target age group of four to eight, and confirmed that the case only needs to fit the Learnly seven-inch tablet. In brainstorming, the industrial designer stressed drop protection using rubber or foam with thick corners. The team discussed a carrying handle, a handle that folds into a stand, bright colours that still appeal to parents, swappable covers, a screen flap versus a raised lip, easy cleaning, and a name tag window. The project manager then assigned the preparation tasks for the functional design meeting.
  decisions: The target group is children aged four to eight. The case only has to fit the company's Learnly seven-inch tablet; there is no universal fit. The case should be made of an easy-to-clean, wipeable material.
  actions: The marketing expert will research what parents and teachers want from the case, possibly with a short survey. The user interface designer will look at the functional side of the case, including the handle and access to the buttons and charging port. The industrial designer will research drop test standards and impact ratings. The user interface designer offered to do this first, but the industrial designer took it. The industrial designer will look into materials (rubber, foam, plastics) that fit the budget. The project manager will write up the minutes and send them round. Someone should check the retail prices of existing children's tablet cases. Nobody took this task.
  problems: It is unclear whether the 25 Euro price is competitive, because no one knows what competing cases cost, and no one was assigned to find out. The 12.50 Euro cost limit may rule out features that add parts, such as swappable covers. Whether the handle should double as a stand is open. The user interface designer worried that a foldable stand could pinch children's fingers. The name tag window idea was parked without a decision. The wide four-to-eight age range covers users with quite different needs.
  action item SY0209a.ai1: Research what parents and teachers want from a children's tablet case, possibly via a short survey (owner B, active)
  action item SY0209a.ai2: Work out the functional side of the case: how children use it, the handle, and access to the buttons and charging port (owner C, active)
  action item SY0209a.ai3: Look into drop tests: the heights competing cases are rated for and the relevant impact standards (owner D, active)
  action item SY0209a.ai4: Investigate materials (rubber, foam, plastics) that fit the production budget (owner D, active)
  action item SY0209a.ai5: Write up the meeting minutes and send them to the team (owner A, active)
  action item SY0209a.ai6: Check the retail prices of existing children's tablet cases (owner no owner, active)
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a carrying handle; it was not decided.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert suggested that the handle fold out into a stand; it was kept as an idea only, because of a finger-pinching concern.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested swappable colour covers; the industrial designer objected on cost.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert suggested a screen flap; the user interface designer doubted it would survive young children, and the discussion moved to a raised lip around the screen.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a name tag window; it was parked without agreement.

[SY0209b, functional design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the functional design meeting and noted that the marketing expert was absent through illness. She confirmed she had sent round the kickoff minutes and reported early survey feedback from the marketing expert, which pointed to drop protection and easy cleaning as parents' main concerns. The industrial designer presented his drop test research, and the team set a drop rating target of 1.2 metres; he then compared silicone, polycarbonate and EVA foam, and the team chose EVA foam for the body. The user interface designer presented the functional design, covering a carrying handle, covered power and volume buttons, an open charging port, a camera cut-out and a raised lip around the screen. The team rejected the fold-out stand because of the finger-pinching risk and chose a fixed moulded handle. The team also dropped swappable covers, and the task of checking competitor prices moved from the user interface designer to the absent marketing expert.
  decisions: The case should survive a drop of 1.2 metres. The case body will be made of EVA foam with thick corners. The power and volume buttons will be covered by press-through foam bumps, the charging port will be an open cut-out, and there will be a cut-out for the rear camera. The screen will be protected by a raised lip rather than a flap. The case will have a fixed handle moulded into the foam, with no fold-out stand. Swappable covers are dropped because of the budget.
  actions: The marketing expert will send the full survey results to the team before the next meeting. The marketing expert will check the retail prices of existing children's tablet cases. This task was first given to the user interface designer and then reassigned. The user interface designer will sketch the fixed handle and the positions of the cut-outs. The industrial designer will get a supplier quote for the whole EVA foam case, including the handle and the raised lip. The project manager will write up and send round the minutes. The project manager will email the marketing expert about his tasks and about the decision against the fold-out stand. The industrial designer's task of costing a hinge for a fold-out stand was dropped once the stand was rejected.
  problems: Only about a dozen survey responses have come in so far. It is still unknown whether 25 Euros is a competitive price. The price check now sits with the absent marketing expert, and it is unclear whether he can finish it before the next meeting. Whether to give the back of the case a wedge shape so it can stand up was deferred to the conceptual design meeting, because of concerns about extra foam and weight. The name tag window is still undecided and waits on teacher feedback from the survey. Colours were not discussed and were deferred to the next meeting. The marketing expert has not yet been told that his fold-out stand idea was rejected.
  action item SY0209b.ai1: Check the retail prices of existing children's tablet cases in the main shops (owner B, reassigned)
  action item SY0209b.ai2: Send the full parent and teacher survey results to the team before the next meeting (owner B, active)
  action item SY0209b.ai3: Find out what a hinge for a fold-out handle stand would cost (owner D, dropped)
  action item SY0209b.ai4: Sketch the fixed handle and the positions of the button, port and camera cut-outs (owner C, active)
  action item SY0209b.ai5: Get a supplier quote for the whole EVA foam case, including the handle and the raised lip (owner D, active)
  action item SY0209b.ai6: Write up the meeting minutes and send them round (owner A, active)
  action item SY0209b.ai7: Email the marketing expert about his assigned tasks and the decision against the fold-out stand (owner A, active)
  fact (absence): The marketing expert, Tomasz, was absent from the functional design meeting because he was off sick.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a wedge-shaped back so the case can stand up; it was deferred to the conceptual design meeting.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer again proposed a name tag window for schools; it was left undecided until the survey results come in.
  fact (plan_change): The competitor price check was first given to the user interface designer and then reassigned to the marketing expert, because it is a marketing task.
  fact (action_item_removed): The industrial designer's task of costing a hinge for the fold-out stand was dropped after the stand was rejected.

[SY0209c, conceptual design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the conceptual design meeting and welcomed back the marketing expert, who confirmed that he had received her email and the minutes and accepted that his fold-out stand had been rejected because of the finger-pinching risk. The marketing expert presented 31 survey responses from 23 parents and 8 teachers. Drop protection and easy cleaning were the top concerns, followed by the handle. Most teachers wanted a way to tell cases apart, and parents wanted bright colours that do not show dirt. His price check found children's tablet cases selling for about 12 to 30 Euros, with branded foam cases with handles at 20 to 28 Euros, so 25 Euros is within the range but at the upper end. The industrial designer reported a supplier quote of 8.40 Euros per case for the EVA foam case with the handle and raised lip, and said a second colour adds about 0.30 Euros. The user interface designer presented sketches of a fixed loop handle on the top edge and the positions of the button, charging port and camera cut-outs. The team agreed on a shallow wedge-shaped back and agreed in principle on a name tag window if it costs under one Euro. They chose strong blue and lime green as the two launch colours and set aside a third colour and a stylus slot. The estimated cost is 9.30 Euros plus the name tag window, so even with a one-Euro window the case stays at about 10.30 Euros, within the 12.50 Euro limit.
  decisions: The back of the case will have a shallow wedge at the bottom so the case can stand up. It adds about 0.60 Euros and about 40 grams, and gives extra foam at the bottom corners. The team agreed in principle to include a name tag window on the back, provided it costs under one Euro. The case will launch in two colours, a strong blue and a lime green.
  actions: The industrial designer will find out what the name tag window costs, as a clear insert or as a moulded foam pocket with clear film, and will get a revised supplier quote that includes the wedge back and the second colour. The user interface designer offered to price the window insert, but the industrial designer took the task because he is already talking to the supplier. The user interface designer will update her sketches to show the wedge back and the name tag window. The marketing expert will draw up criteria, based on the survey, for evaluating the final design. The project manager will write up the minutes. Someone should check whether the case counts as a toy under children's product safety rules. Nobody took this task.
  problems: At 25 Euros the case sits at the upper end of the competitor price range, so it needs an extra feature such as the name tag window to justify the price. The cost of the name tag window is still unknown, and a separate plastic window part could crack. The supplier asked whether the case is sold as a toy, which would bring extra safety rules for children's products, possibly affecting small parts like the window. Nobody took on checking this. The user interface designer's suggestions of a third colour (orange) and a stylus slot were not adopted. The third colour was turned down because each colour needs its own minimum order, and the stylus slot because it would weaken the side wall.
  action item SY0209c.ai1: Find out the cost of the name tag window (clear insert or moulded foam pocket with clear film) and get a revised supplier quote including the wedge back and the second colour (owner D, active)
  action item SY0209c.ai2: Check whether the case counts as a toy under children's product safety rules (owner no owner, active)
  action item SY0209c.ai3: Update the sketches to show the wedge back and the name tag window (owner C, active)
  action item SY0209c.ai4: Put together criteria, based on the survey, for evaluating the final design (owner B, active)
  action item SY0209c.ai5: Write up the meeting minutes (owner A, active)
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a third colour, orange. The industrial designer and the marketing expert preferred to keep two colours for launch because each colour needs its own minimum order.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested a stylus slot on the side. It was left aside because it would weaken the side wall and few young children use a stylus.
  fact (plan_change): The user interface designer offered to look into the cost of the name tag window insert, but the industrial designer took the task because he was already talking to the supplier.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F2_REASSIGNED_OR_DROPPED [F2]: A task is assigned early in the meeting and later in the same meeting is either reassigned to someone else (status reassigned, owner = new owner, previous_owners lists the original) or dropped entirely (status dropped).
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.
- F2_TASK_TO_ABSENT [F2]: A task is assigned to a team member who is absent from this meeting. The gold action item owner is that absent participant.
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
